props.gloss_en: circumcision overrides [the prohibition of cutting] leprosy, both in its time and not in its time
a Festival it overrides -- in its time
a Festival it does not override except in its time alone

'the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised' -- even if there is a baheret there, he cuts; 'take heed in the plague of leprosy' is for other places; the verse says 'flesh': even if there is a baheret there
(the rival) or perhaps [take heed applies] even to circumcision, and 'he shall circumcise' means when there is no baheret
Rava: the tanna first held it by kal vachomer from Shabbat; 'or perhaps' is his reconsidering: whence that Shabbat is graver? perhaps leprosy is, for it overrides the service
another version: the tanna's first reason was that an aseh overrides a lav; 'or perhaps' is his reconsidering: that is said of a bare lav, and this is an aseh and a lav
granted for an adult, of whom 'flesh' is written
an infant too -- 'flesh' is written of him
Abaye: their common factor is that they are circumcised and override leprosy; so all who are circumcised override leprosy -- the intermediate child included
Rava: that circumcision in its time overrides [leprosy] needs no verse; it comes by kal vachomer

Rav Ashi: an aseh overrides a lav only where, at the moment the lav is uprooted, the aseh is fulfilled -- as circumcision with leprosy, or tzitzit with kilayim; here, when the lav is uprooted the aseh is not fulfilled
and this [dispute] of Rava and Rav Safra is a dispute of tannaim
R' Yoshiya: 'flesh' -- even if there is a baheret there, he circumcises
R' Yonatan: it is not needed -- Shabbat, which is grave, [circumcision] overrides; leprosy, all the more so
